meaning.en: Type 1 AC connector (SAE J1772, IEC 62196-2 Type 1; North America, Japan), shown as the vehicle inlet face
meaning.de: Typ-1-AC-Stecker (SAE J1772, IEC 62196-2 Typ 1; Nordamerika, Japan), dargestellt als Fahrzeug-Ladebuchse in Draufsicht

standard.source: SAE J1772 and IEC 62196-2 themselves not consulted. Layout checked against three public drawings on Wikimedia Commons, retrieved 2026-11-02: "File:J1772 connector.svg" by Mliu92 (CC BY-SA 4.0; "view facing the plug end", i.e. the face of the cable connector, drawn approximately to scale, 10 px = 1 mm: round face, L1 and N large at the top left and right, PP and CP small at the lower left and right, PE large at the bottom centre; relative to the face radius R the contacts sit at (±0.38, −0.33) R, (±0.52, +0.27) R and (0, +0.52) R), https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:J1772_connector.svg; "File:SAE J1772 Type 1.png" (Schneider Electric, CC BY 3.0; connector face with latch at the top, same arrangement: two large contacts at the top, two small ones at the sides, one large at the bottom centre), https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:SAE_J1772_Type_1.png; and "File:Type1 J1772.svg" by GreatDrok (CC BY-SA 4.0; unlabelled, same arrangement), https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Type1_J1772.svg. The drawings show the connector face; the icon shows the vehicle inlet seen from the front, which is its mirror image (N top left, L1 top right, CP lower left, PP lower right). Because L1 and N have the same size, and PP and CP too, the mirrored face looks the same. Contact positions are the Mliu92 positions scaled to R 9. Drawn: the face outline (latch and keying tab omitted, too fine), L1, N and PE as rings r 1.5, PP and CP as dots (the drawing's 4.5 mm signal pins against 6 mm power pins; plain dots keep the two sizes apart at 16 px).
